answer: The tide hands the epoch's sole signing duty to one vertex: an agent is born only when that vertex signs its pulse, one pulse per epoch. That vertex locks base×c² of its own on the birth, c its lifetime birth count, forfeit whole on any fake, and sells the rung to the buyer. Split wallets buy nothing: the pen is one per epoch and even a fresh vertex is minted through it, so an operator's k clones queue serially and its k-th clone pays the cheapest rung — base×c², with c pushed up by its own earlier births — after k idle turns of the tide. A newcomer takes the first rung on its first turn.
